predecessors.name: Eastern Turkic Khaganate (Eastern Göktürks)
predecessors.text: the steppe between the Yellow River and the Gobi where Taizong had settled the Turks

predecessors.name: Tang dynasty
predecessors.text: the Tang frontier land from which Ilterish 'rose up in arms against the Tang authorities' after the failed rebellions of Ashina Nishufu (679-680) and Ashina Funian (680-681)

successors.name: Uyghur Khaganate
successors.text: Otuken, seized by Kutlug in 744; the Uyghurs killed Kulun Beg in 745

successors.name: Yenisei Kyrgyz
successors.text: the Sayan and Tannu-Ola country of the Kyrgyz, whom the Turks had crushed in 709-710

successors.name: Türgesh Khaganate
successors.text: the western marches around the Bolchu river

ledger.x: 682: Ilterish raises the Turkic banner against the Tang.
692: Qapaghan becomes qaghan and the khaganate holds the plateau of Mongolia.
709-710: the Turks crush the Yenisei Kyrgyz.
711: Tonyukuk crushes the Turgesh at the Bolchu river.
711: after Bolchu 'all western Turkestan came under the Second Turkic Khaganate'.
713-714: the Turks fall back from Transoxiana.
22 July 716: Qapaghan is killed on his way home from suppressing the Tiele, and the push in the west ends.
745: the Khitan tie ends with the khaganate.
745: the Kyrgyz tie ends with the khaganate.
745: the last Gokturk khagan is killed.

wars.name: Turkic rebellions against the Tang (679-683)
wars.outcome: Nishufu (679-680) and Funian (680-681) failed; Ilterish rose in 682, raided Lan Prefecture in 683 and restored the khaganate.

wars.name: Qapaghan's wars with the Tang
wars.outcome: Raids: Ling Prefecture 694, the Khitan base 697, Dingzhou and Zhao Prefecture in August 698, six crossings of the Yellow River between 693 and 706, Lingwu in 705.

wars.name: Battle of Bolchu
wars.outcome: Tonyukuk crushed the Turgesh in 711, killing Saqal and Zhenu; the Turgesh recovered under Suluk.

wars.name: Fall of the Second Turkic Khaganate
wars.outcome: The Basmyls, Karluks and Uyghurs destroyed the khaganate in 744; Kulun Beg was beheaded in 745.

certainty.note: A steppe khaganate: the pages describe its frontiers by mountain ranges (Tannu Ola, Altai, Tarbagatai), the upper Kerulen and Lake Baikal; no treaty line.
